name: Arrays
intro: The base of everything. 14 patterns, mostly about scanning smarter than a double loop.

name: Strings
intro: A string is an array of characters. Most array patterns carry over, plus a few string-only ones.

name: Linked List
intro: No random access, so every trick is about pointers: moving them at different speeds, reversing them, or anchoring them with a dummy node.

name: Stack
intro: Last in, first out. Use it when the most recent unfinished item must be handled first.

name: Queue / Deque
intro: First in, first out (queue), or add/remove at both ends (deque).

name: HashMap / HashSet
intro: Trade memory for speed: O(1) average lookup turns many O(n²) searches into O(n).

name: Recursion
intro: A function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller one. Backtracking is recursion that tries, then undoes.

name: Binary Tree
intro: Each node has at most two children. Nearly every problem is a traversal with a small twist.

name: Binary Search Tree
intro: A binary tree where left < node < right holds for every node. That ordering gives O(h) search, and sorted inorder.

name: Heap / Priority Queue
intro: Gives the smallest (or largest) item in O(1) and removes it in O(log n). Use it when you keep asking for "the best so far".

name: Graph
intro: Nodes and edges. Most problems hide a graph: grids, dependencies, word ladders, networks.

name: Greedy
intro: Make the locally best choice at each step and never look back. It only works when a local best leads to a global best.

name: Dynamic Programming
intro: Recursion + remembering. If a problem has overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure, solve each subproblem once.

name: Trie (prefix tree)
intro: A tree where each edge is a character, so words sharing a prefix share a path. Prefix questions cost O(length of word), not O(number of words).

name: Bit Manipulation
intro: Work directly on the binary digits. Fast, O(1) space, and the source of many neat tricks.
